description: Count exact-length legal no-repeat patterns on the canonical 3x3 Android grid.

source.discovery_note: Codewars public title and tags only; no task content used.
source.method_source: Uellenbeck et al., Quantifying the Security of Graphical Passwords: The Case of Android Unlock Patterns; Lee et al., A Visibility-Based Lower Bound for Android Unlock Patterns

input.grid: fixed 3x3; points numbered 0..8 in row-major order

output.encoding: exact number of valid ordered patterns using exactly L distinct points

pattern_rules: No point is used more than once.
Each move is a straight segment between grid points.
Every grid point strictly inside a move segment must have appeared earlier in the pattern.
contract.primary_method: Depth-first enumeration from each possible start with a 9-bit visited mask and a midpoint visibility test before every extension.
contract.independent_method: Scan all length-L permutations of the nine points and check each segment's interior lattice points against the visited prefix using a gcd-derived step vector.
contract.invalid_cases: Null input, non-exact framing, or L outside 4..9 returns -1.
contract.distinct_from: Ordinary simple-path and Hamiltonian-path packages have static edge availability and do not enforce the state-dependent skipped-midpoint rule.

complexity.primary_time: O(9!) in the worst case; depth-first prefixes use constant work per candidate move.
complexity.primary_space: O(L) recursion frames and a 9-bit visited mask.
complexity.independent_time: At most 9! candidate permutations, with at most 8 transitions and one interior-point check per transition.
complexity.independent_space: O(L) for one candidate pattern and its visited-point set.
